newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Dardanel targets $100 mln sales in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Dardanel targets $100 mln sales in 1997.

text.p: Turkey's leading frozen and canned food producer Dardanel Onentas Gida Sanayi A.S. targets $100 million turnover in 1997, while preparing to enter the growing Turkish pet-food market as the first domestic producer, a senior company official said.
"Our 1997 budget program is based on $60 million of exports and $40 million of domestic sales," Osman Niyazi Onen, president and general manager of the company, told Reuters.
He said a total sales figure of slightly above $60 million was awaited in 1996, including more than $30 million of exports.
Dardanel shares traded at 2,025 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange on Friday, up from Thursday's 2,000 lira close.
The company completed a $15 million investment on modernisation and capacity expansion of its tuna fish processing lines in September and doubled the daily processing capacity to 200 tonnes.
"With the new production lines we have the capabiliy of realising $200 million of annual sales and our 1998 target is to reach $150 million of sales with new products," Onen said.
"After 1998 we will concentrate on catching the $200 million sales figure by utilising the idle capacity during the off-seasons and without any new investment," he added.
Dardanel began producing pet food for cats in September using the black flesh of the tuna fish, which had been wasted before. The product is currently exported to England and Japan.
Onen said they would introduce three types of pet food for cats on to the domestic market with a new brand in November, in coordination with an English company, which he declined to name.
He said they would be the first domestic pet-food producer in the Turkish market, which would give them price advantage.
The company recently introduced to Turkey the so-called "Quickburger", a hamburger which can be cooked in a microwave oven. It is sold at 1,000 outlets throughout the country.
"Now we are concentrating on a new project to produce tiny pizzas to be sold at the same sales points with Quickburger," Onen said.
He said they would also enter the Turkish sauce and instant soup market in 1997 to utilise the idle capacity.
Dardanel began producing fish flour in late summer, after completing its $1.2 million investment, which was the last step of its project to utilise raw tuna fish completely.

Inspired by the ancient Greek poet Homer, who eulogised mussels from the Dardanelles, the company said it planned to set up a mussel farm on the Dardanelles strait to produce upto 2,000 tonnes of frozen and canned mussels annually for international and domestic markets.
The company imports all packaging cans from Italy in printed, curved and pressed form, but Onen complained about the high transportation costs and said:
"We are planing to set up a tin curving and pressing line next year. So, importing just printed tin will be enough for us which will reduce the can costs."

Dardanel reported 186.8 billion lira of provisional net profits and 3.2 trillion lira of net sales in January-September 1996, up from 160.9 billion lira and 2.4 trillion lira, respectively in the same 1995 period. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
